messages.text: OK so we need to design a REST API for a food delivery app. Let me start.
First, we need a users endpoint. POST /api/users for registration, GET /api/users/:id for profile.
Then restaurants. GET /api/restaurants for listing, GET /api/restaurants/:id for details, POST /api/restaurants for adding new ones.
That makes sense.
For orders, we need POST /api/orders to create, GET /api/orders/:id to track, PUT /api/orders/:id/status to update.
The menu should be nested under restaurants. GET /api/restaurants/:id/menu returns the full menu.
Yeah, that's right.
For authentication, JWT tokens. Login returns a token, every subsequent request includes it in the Authorization header.
Payment integration would be POST /api/payments with the order ID and payment method. Stripe or Razorpay.
Sounds good to me.
For real-time tracking, we could use WebSockets. The delivery person sends location updates, and the customer gets them in real-time.
The order status flow would be: placed → confirmed → preparing → picked_up → delivered.
What about cancellation? Can users cancel after the order is confirmed?
Good question. Cancel should only work before 'preparing' status. POST /api/orders/:id/cancel with a check on current status.
We also need ratings. POST /api/orders/:id/rating after delivery. Rating for both restaurant and delivery person.
Search endpoint: GET /api/restaurants/search?q=pizza&lat=28.7&lng=77.1&radius=5km
Should we use geospatial queries for that? Like MongoDB's $near?
Yes, MongoDB with 2dsphere index would work perfectly for location-based search. Good point Anil.
For the response format, every API should return { success: boolean, data: {}, error: string }. Consistent structure.
Pagination for listings: GET /api/restaurants?page=1&limit=20&sort=rating. Default limit 20, max 50.
What about filtering restaurants by cuisine type?
Add it as query param: GET /api/restaurants?cuisine=indian&veg=true&priceRange=low. Multiple filters.
Rate limiting is important too. 100 requests per minute per user. 429 Too Many Requests if exceeded.
For the delivery person app, separate endpoints: GET /api/delivery/available-orders, POST /api/delivery/accept/:orderId.
Should delivery persons have their own authentication or share the same system?
Same JWT system but with role-based access control. Roles: customer, restaurant_owner, delivery_person, admin.
Middleware checks the role claim in the JWT. Restaurant endpoints only accessible to restaurant_owner role.
Makes sense. Clean architecture.
I think we've covered the main endpoints. Let me write the full API spec in the code editor.
Looks comprehensive. Good job Raj.
Yeah, this is a solid API design.
Thanks team. Let me also add webhook endpoints for payment confirmations and order status changes.
